messages.body_plain:
Hi Elena,

> For 3) I know that there is inactivity time, but I really would like to have the sedentary time.

As explained in other recent threads sedentary behaviour measurement is a myth. Research tools typically either estimate time spent with thigh horizontal which could be sitting or lying or time spent below an acceleration threshold.

In GGIR we call it inactivity because we only look at the acceleration threshold, this to avoid the misleading impression that we are attempting to detect when people have their thigh horizontal. Nonetheless, most publications that have used GGIR refer to these estimates as sedentary behaviour because of peer-pressure in the research community to stick to popular terminology. However, in GGIR we try to avoid using the term sedentary behaviour.

So, if you want to extract the thing that others who have used wrist-accelerometry call sedentary behaviour then you will have to use the inactivity estimates.

I see you have a lot of question. You may want to consider signing up to our GGIR training course where we provide an overview of all there is to know about GGIR: https://www.accelting.com/ggir-training/

Best wishes,

Vincent

Hello Joanna,

> Does anyone know how the ActCR package handles invalid or missing data?

As of the ActCR release from May 2022 (0.3.0) cosinor and extended cosinor analyses are flexible to handle both time series with missing data and with imputed data. I had the same concern as you and this is why I made that contribution to the ActCR code.

Inside GGIR, ActCR is used for cosinor and extended cosinor analyses where invalid time points are set to NA and by that ignored. This is also discussed in the GGIR vignette: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#5102_Cosinor_analysis_and_Extended_Cosinor_analysis

Note that even if a day has less than 16 valid hours GGIR will use the available valid data points for the cosinor analyses.

Best, Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jairo and Puchen,

If you set the mvpa threshold at a level that is indicative of vigorous activity then your MVPA bouts estimates will reflect vigorous activity bouts. If you additionally set the light activity threshold at moderate level, your LIPA bouts will reflect MPA bouts. The main challenge for you is to be aware of this new interpretation of the variable names.

However, this comes at the cost of LIPA being merged with inactivity.
To address that you could run GGIR separately with normal thresholds to extract the relative contribution of LIPA and inactivity and translate those to the analyses above.

My proposal would be to first prove the scientific relevance of capturing all these bout  types via the approach I have described above before we consider adding this to GGIR.

Best,

Vincent

Finally, note also that you have overwrite = FALSE in your script, if you are trying to re-process files that were already processed in the past, you should set this to TRUE.

Jairo

messages.body_plain:
Hi Javad,

Good question. I am currently involved in a study that looks into this and we hope to submit our work to a journal this summer... so my hands are bit tight to answer this in detail. However, I can say the following:

GGIR has been designed to be minimally sensitive to sample frequency. For example, GGIR does not attempt to rely on specific very short lasting events or high frequency signal components. Also, GGIR intentionally does not attempt to detect patterns in the raw data.

The real problem, I think, is that a few accelerometer brands are poor at capturing the acceleration of movement consistently across sample frequency settings. Therefore, I think your question should be accelerometer brand specific.

You give the impression that resampling is a solution to a lack of comparability of raw data, but resampling itself can also introduce discrepancies and on top of that resampling does not address a systematic bias caused by sampling rate. For example, if X Hertz results in 10% lower magnitude of acceleration then resampling will not be able to fix that. A better solution would be to either identify the source of the bias and address it, or to identify problematic accelerometer brand and sample rate combinations and discourage their use.

Kind regards,

Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Hi Elena,

GGIR part 2 provides time spent per intensity level per segment of the day (argument ilevels and qwindow), but does not consider the concept of bouted and unbouted behaviour. Bouted and unbouted behaviour is currently only extracted in part 5 for the waking hours as a whole.

So, I think your question is whether bouts in inactivity, LIPA, etc can be derived with GGIR?
Answer: This is not possible at the moment. Technically it would be possible but that would require a significant time investment, which is hard for me or Jairo to do on a voluntary basis.

Possible solutions:
You find someone to develop this and make a GitHub pull request.
You hire us to develop this. In that case I would be happy to discuss details and provide a quote via email or a call.

Kind regards,

Vincent
